name: r5-m03
statement: The top-8 singular directions per layer matrix of the Olmo-3.1 RL-Zero-Math weight change act like the opening cue: they switch the base into the deliberative 'Okay' register and nothing more, without RL's longer checking policy. So base + top8 on the plain prompt writes answers of the cued base's length and makes the cued base's quick finished-wrong errors, and adding the cue on top of top8 adds almost nothing.
scope: Covers allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B with the top-8 SVD directions per matrix of (Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math minus base) added in (the WSP-1 top8 edit), on MATH-500 at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, compared with the cued base (T1) and RL plain (T2) at the same setting. It does not cover: the harder 328 (where RL's long checking may matter more), T 0.6 (where the cued base loops), other ranks (top1, top64, bulk), the Think-SFT or Code-RL deltas, or why bulk (RL minus top8) also works. That bulk result is redundancy, which this theory does not explain. It also does not claim that top8's wrong set overlaps T1's beyond item difficulty (see conflicts).

imports.finding: A small RL-trained steering vector closes most of the base-to-RL gap by acting as a token-substitution bias on the first generated token. Prefixing that token ('To') to the prompt gives about 75% of the vector's gain.
imports.how: Supplies the mechanism type: a low-rank RL component whose job is to choose the opening and register, which equals a text prefix. Here the top-8 directions are that component and the three-token cue ' line!\n\nOkay' is the equivalent prefix. So the edit and the cue should not add up.

explains.how: The plain base's 224 is a register failure. The top-8 edit supplies the cue's register on the plain prompt and lands near the cued base's 405-418 rather than at RL's 463.
Top8 plain writes 3,962 tokens per problem: the cued base's length, not RL's. The edit copies the mode but not RL's longer checking.

explains.quote: Late-MLP top directions x base lm_head read as deliberation words
explains.how: The top directions read out 'Okay'/'Wait'/'consider', the cue's own opening words, which is what a register switch would look like in the weights.

explains.quote: The opening cue is the RL model's own
explains.how: Because the cue is RL's own opening, the RL delta must encode that opening, and its largest directions are where a cheap opening switch would sit.

explains.quote: base + those 8 directions plain 427 vs matched random 197
explains.how: The effect is specific to the real directions, not to the edit's energy, as expected if those directions carry a definite behaviour (the mode switch).

conflicts.quote: Arms that recover accuracy also adopt RL's format and length
conflicts.how: In n13 at T 0.6, every recovering arm took RL's length. This theory says the top-8 arm recovers accuracy at the cued base's length instead. The two can both hold only if the n13 arms (full-rank pieces of the delta) carried more than the mode switch.

conflicts.quote: mean excess union of -0.05 problems over the difficulty-matched null
conflicts.how: Arms share errors only as much as item difficulty predicts, so 'top8 errs where the cued base errs' cannot mean an overlap beyond difficulty. The theory keeps only the weaker claim that top8 makes base-type errors.
RL without its top-8 directions still scores high on the plain prompt, so the mode switch is not held only in the top 8. The theory does not explain this redundancy.

rival: The strongest rival is a partial dose: top8 is a weaker copy of the whole RL policy, sitting between theta(0.25) plain (405, 3,653 tokens) and theta(0.5) plain (443, 4,536 tokens) on the dose line, so it carries some of RL's checking and length. Two observations separate them. (a) Adding the cue: on the dose line the cue still adds points (theta0.25 405 -> 441, theta0.5 443 -> 452), so the rival puts top8 + cue near 440-450; this theory puts it at top8's plain score (~425). (b) Short wrong answers: RL's checking removes them (RL answers <= 4,000 tokens: 0 wrong), so the rival predicts few, while this theory predicts about as many as the cued base has.

predictions.experiment: Per-problem log length ratio of top8 plain to the cued base, ln(top8 n_generated / T1 tokens), taken as the median over problems. This tests the mechanism. This theory says top8 has the cued base's length, so the median is near 0 (slightly positive if top8 has fewer cap hits). The nearest rival (knowledge-69adda / r1-surprises-2: recovering arms take RL's length) says top8 has RL's length. It predicts the same statistic computed with t2_generated_tokens in place of top8, about 0.6.
predictions.recipe: Load studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/top8_plain-01/per_problem.json and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. Join on problem_index and keep the problems present in both (drop missing rows). For each problem compute ln(max(n_generated,1) / max(t1_generated_tokens,1)), with n_generated from the top8 file. Keep cap hits, at their stored token counts. Report the median over the joined problems. If the count is even, the median is the mean of the two middle values.

predictions.experiment: Count of quick finished-wrong answers in top8 plain: answers wrong under v3, not cap hits, and at most 2,000 generated tokens. This tests whether the edit carries RL's checking policy. This theory (base-type errors without RL's checking) predicts about the cued base's count (T1 has 13 wrong among its 263 answers of <= 2,000 tokens). The RL-checking rival predicts 0-3 (RL has 0 wrong among answers of <= 4,000 tokens). The partial-dose rival predicts about 5.
predictions.recipe: Load studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/top8_plain-01/per_problem.json. Count the rows with score_v3 == 0, cap_hit false and n_generated <= 2000. Rows with a missing score_v3 are left out. Each problem_index counts once.
predictions.refuted_by: count at most 4 or at least 23

predictions.experiment: Fraction of the cued base's wrong problems (T1 wrong) that top8 plain also gets wrong.
predictions.recipe: Join studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json with studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/full500/top8_plain-01/per_problem.json on problem_index. Keep the problems with t1_right false (a T1 cap hit counts as wrong) that are present in both files. Report the fraction of those whose top8 score_v3 == 0. A top8 cap hit counts as wrong. Problems missing from the top8 file are dropped.

predictions.experiment: New GPU cell: base + top-8 directions per matrix of the RL-Math delta (the WSP-1 top8 edit, jobs/wsp_edit.py), WITH the opening cue ids [1584, 2268, 33413] after the prompt. MATH-500, n = 500, 1 sample, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, seed base 184,000,000, one H100 (about 2M tokens, about 35-40 min). This theory says the cue is redundant with the edit, so the score stays at top8 plain's level. The partial-dose rival predicts the cue still adds, as on the theta line, giving about 440-450.
predictions.refuted_by: top8 + cue scores 441 or more of 500 (the cue adds on top of the edit), or below 405
